title: K-flat tensor with a degree-zero module on a ringed site
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site essentially small in a coefficient universe $w$ [def-weil-size-convention], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with values in $w$. Use sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and the localization $Q_R$ to their unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Give $D(R)$ the K-flat derived tensor of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], for the sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $P$ be any K-flat cochain complex [def-pc-kflat-complex], and let $M$ be any sheaf of $R$-modules. Write $M[0]$ for its complex concentrated in degree zero and define the termwise tensor complex $T_M(P)$ by
$$T_M(P)^q=P^q\otimes_R M,\qquad d_{T_M(P)}^q=d_P^q\otimes1_M.$$
There is a canonical isomorphism
$$c_{P,M}:Q_R(P)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_R(M[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_R(T_M(P)).$$
It is natural in chain maps between K-flat complexes and in module-sheaf maps: for $u:P\to P'$ and $f:M\to M'$, its naturality square has right-hand map $Q_R(T(u,f))$, where $T(u,f)^q=u^q\otimes f$. The comparison is the one induced by the K-flat resolution construction and the degree-zero total-tensor identification, and is independent of auxiliary resolutions. Neither boundedness nor flatness of the individual terms of $P$, nor flatness of $M$, is required.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ in the coefficient universe $w$, using the small skeleton prescribed by [def-weil-size-convention]. The Grothendieck assertion of [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] applies to this small ringed site. By [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], its sheafified tensor is symmetric monoidal, closed and additive in both variables. By [lem-trf-site-functorial-flat-resolution], it has functorial flat resolutions without identifying the site and coefficient universes. These verify every categorical hypothesis of the general derived-monoidal theorem used below; no condition on $M$ or the terms of $P$ has been introduced.

proof.text: The K-flatness convention in the general theorem is [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. It agrees here with [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Indeed, the latter implies that $f\otimes1_P$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every quasi-isomorphism $f$, by [lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent]. For the other order use the symmetry of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]: on the degree-$(i,j)$ summand the signed swap is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$. The total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives coefficients $(-1)^{ij}$ on $d y\otimes x$ and $(-1)^{ij+j}$ on $y\otimes d x$ in both composites with this swap. Thus it is a natural chain isomorphism, so $1_P\otimes f$ is conjugate to $f\otimes1_P$ and is a quasi-isomorphism. Conversely, apply preservation to $0\to X$ for an acyclic $X$: its tensor with $P$ is $0\to\operatorname{Tot}(X\otimes P)$, so that total complex is acyclic. This also checks that both conventions use the identical signed direct-sum total tensor.

source.place: Tags 06YN and 06YP, definition-K-flat and lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism; signed symmetry calculation for the two K-flat conventions

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] to $\mathcal A$. Denote its derived tensor by $B$ and the multiplication of its lax localization by $\mu_{X,Y}:B(Q_RX,Q_RY)\to Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(X\otimes_RY)$. The theorem says that $B$ is the two-variable left derived tensor and is computed by replacing either argument by a K-flat resolution; consequently $\mu_{X,Y}$ is an isomorphism whenever $X$ is K-flat, with $Y$ arbitrary. In particular the identity resolution $P\to P$ computes $\mu_{P,Y}$ for every $Y$. The multiplication is a natural transformation in both homotopy-category variables, so its naturality also holds for every pair of chain maps.

source.place: Derived tensor theorem: two-variable left derived tensor, computation by either K-flat argument, and lax localization

proof.text: Write $T$ for the tensor fixed in the statement. For flat-term K-flat $A,B$, let $\beta_{A,B}:Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_RB)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(Q_RA,Q_RB)$ be the natural comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. On these pairs $\beta_{A,B}\mu_{A,B}$ is a natural isomorphism from the restriction of the bifunctor $B$ of step 3 to that of $T$. The transformation-extension clause of that node extends it uniquely to $\theta:B\xrightarrow{\sim}T$: extend its inverse too; the two composites restrict to identities and hence are identities by the uniqueness clause. Define $m_{X,Y}=\mu_{X,Y}\theta^{-1}_{Q_RX,Q_RY}$. This is natural for chain maps and is invertible when $X$ is K-flat. Its normalization is $m_{A,B}=\beta_{A,B}^{-1}$ on flat-term K-flat pairs. Thus this uses precisely the tensor $T$ named in the item.

source.place: Compare the two-variable derived tensor with the specified flat-term K-flat descent, using its extension and uniqueness clauses

proof.text: For every $P,M$ there is a chain isomorphism $\delta_{P,M}:\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RM[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}T_M(P)$. In degree $q$, every summand indexed by $(i,j)$ with $j\ne0$ is zero, while the sole remaining summand has $(i,j)=(q,0)$ and is $P^q\otimes_RM$. Projection to that summand and its inclusion are inverse. The differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] on it is $d_P^q\otimes1_M+(-1)^q1\otimes0=d_P^q\otimes1_M$. The map induced by $u$ and $f[0]$ is, on this same summand, $u^q\otimes f$, so $\delta$ is natural in both variables. Set $c_{P,M}=Q_R(\delta_{P,M})\,m_{P,M[0]}$; both factors are isomorphisms by step 4 and the hypothesis that $P$ is K-flat.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor, specialized to degree zero; direct calculation of the total complex

proof.text:
For $u:P\to P'$ and $f:M\to M'$, naturality of the lax-localization multiplication in [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] and of $\theta$ from [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] gives
$$Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(u\otimes f[0])\,m_{P,M[0]}=m_{P',M'[0]}\,T(Q_Ru,Q_R(f[0])).$$
The summand calculation in step 5 gives $\delta_{P',M'}\operatorname{Tot}(u\otimes f[0])=T(u,f)\delta_{P,M}$. Compose these two equations to obtain
$$Q_R(T(u,f))\,c_{P,M}=c_{P',M'}\,T(Q_Ru,Q_R(f[0])),$$
which is exactly the asserted naturality square, including its specified right-hand map.

source.place: Naturality of lax localization and of the uniquely normalized tensor identification

proof.text:
To check the resolution normalization explicitly, choose flat-term K-flat resolutions $p:A\to P$ and $b:B\to M[0]$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Naturality of $m$ and its normalization in step 4 give
$$c_{P,M}\,T(Q_Rp,Q_Rb)\,\beta_{A,B}=Q_R\bigl(\delta_{P,M}\operatorname{Tot}(p\otimes b)\bigr).$$
Here $T(Q_Rp,Q_Rb)\beta_{A,B}$ is an isomorphism: the two resolution maps become isomorphisms under localization, and $\beta$ is the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Hence this equation uniquely determines $c_{P,M}$ and is exactly the computation obtained by resolving both factors and then applying the augmentations and the degree-zero identification. It holds for every such pair of resolutions, so every auxiliary choice yields the same $c_{P,M}$. The either-argument computation of [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] also permits the identity resolution of the already K-flat $P$; it has the same $m_{P,M[0]}$ and hence the same $c_{P,M}$. None of these steps bounds $P$ or assumes its individual terms or $M$ flat.
